before: In the fourth consulship of Valerian and the third of Gallienus, three days before the Kalends of September, at Carthage in the council chamber, Paternus the governor spoke to Cyprian the bishop: "The most sacred emperors Valerian and Gallienus have seen fit to send me a letter, commanding that those who do not practice the Roman religion must perform the Roman worship rites. I have asked about your identity, so what do you answer?"

Cyprian the bishop said: "I am a Christian and a bishop. I know no other gods but the one true God, who made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that is in them. We Christians serve this God, and we pray to him day and night for ourselves and for all people and for the safety of the emperors themselves."
Paternus the governor said: "Do you stand firm in this resolve then?" Cyprian the bishop replied: "A good resolve that knows God cannot be changed."
Paternus the governor said: "Then will you go into exile to the city of Curubis, as Valerian and Gallienus command?" Cyprian the bishop said: "I will go."
